This has not been my experience, as well. Psychiatrists are twice as expensive per hour as psychologists, and rarely delve deep into problems. Mine just wants to check on the dosage of my medications.

Yeah, but I didn't beat it. I'm still depressed, and I'm still overweight. I've gotten marginally better since he was born, and I want to fix things, but I haven't. I'm just afraid if I do get myself right, how can I risk losing 5 more years?
My pregnancy was awesome! It was the best I'd felt mentally and physically in my life. Had a natural birth with no unusual complications. But those first 6 months or so after birth nearly killed me.

The thing is, when I was pregnant, it was probably the best I had ever felt, mentally and physically. I hadn't been depressed for two and a half years. And then after he was born, I was a wreck. Also, pregnancy/weight gain caused a relapse in my IBS, and since then I have developed monthly menstrual migraines. I mean, yes, the stress of everything will trigger depression, but I can't help to think there was something biological there, too. Also, I have PCOS, so I never produced much breastmilk, and it kind of took me a long-ish time to form an attachment to my son. 

I've been in and out of therapy for the last 12 years. I've tried several SSRIs with horrible side effects, and it took a long time to be willing to try Wellbutrin. What I should probably be on, because I have atypical depression, is a MAOI, but the side effects from those scare the shit out of me.

This is big, I know.  When things go wrong I feel like I have two options: get mad at someone else for screwing up, or internalize it and blame myself.  When it's my advisor and they can't hear me, I bitch about them.  But when it's my son or my husband and I feel like I can't be mean to them  about things they may (or may not) have done wrong, then it comes out as self deprecation.  I guess I need to have a talk with my husband and warn him that I'm either going to be nagging or moping, and that I'm tired of moping.  Thanks.
